329499.title: The four-colour conjecture for signed planar graphs
329499.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple signed planar graph, and let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, defined as the smallest $n$ for which $G$ has a proper colouring using colours from $M_n$, where $M_{2k}=\{\pm1,\pm2,\ldots,\pm k\}$ and $M_{2k+1}=\{0,\pm1,\pm2,\ldots,\pm k\}$. **Four-colour conjecture for signed planar graphs.** Every simple signed planar graph $G$ has

$$
\chi(G)\le 4.
$$

The paper proves the corresponding upper bound $\chi(G)\le 5$, as well as the bounds $\chi(G)\le 4$ for triangle-free signed planar graphs and $\chi(G)\le 3$ for signed planar graphs of girth at least $5$. The conjecture asks whether the general bound can be improved to $4$.
329499.findings: Kardos–Narboni arXiv1906.05638 explicitly refutes this exact signed-colour convention. Search located primary abstract; proof body not read, so no construction/fidelity claim beyond the resolution lead.
329499.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Read 1906.05638 if a detailed old-result reconstruction is needed; no discovery work justified.

329517.title: Gyárfás–Györi–Simonovits partition conjecture for 3-uniform hypergraphs
329517.literal_statement: Let $H$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph, and let $b1(H)$ denote the cardinality of a largest independent set of $H$. A **linear cycle** is a sequence of at least three edges in which only cyclically consecutive edges intersect, and consecutive edges intersect in exactly one vertex. **Gyárfás–Györi–Simonovits conjecture.** The vertex set of every $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$ can be partitioned into $b1(H)$ linear cycles, edges, and subsets of hyperedges. This conjecture concerns decomposing the vertices of a hypergraph into pieces controlled by its independence number and linear-cycle structure; the source states that it remains open.
329517.findings: Independence number bounds pieces, not total edges. Greedy deletion of a maximal linear cycle can lower alpha by zero, so induction does not charge one piece.
329517.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Prove a deletion lemma producing a cycle/edge/subedge Q with alpha(H-Q) <= alpha(H)-1. No such lemma proved.

329595.title: Conjecture on cycles in odd-cycle-free graphs
329595.literal_statement:
Let $k>1$, and let $C_{2k+1}$ denote the cycle of length $2k+1$. A graph is **$C_{2k+1}$-free** if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $C_{2k+1}$; $K_{a,b}$ denotes the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $a$ and $b$. **Odd-cycle-free cycle conjecture.** For any $k>1$, if an $n$-vertex $C_{2k+1}$-free graph $G$ has the maximum number of cycles, then

$$
G=K_{\left \lceil \frac{n}{2}\right \rceil,\left \lfloor \frac{n}{2}\right \rfloor}.
$$

The conjecture extends the extremal cycle question from triangle-free graphs to longer odd-cycle exclusions. The surrounding discussion notes related extremal edge and maximal-graph results, but the conjecture's resolution is not supplied.
329595.findings: Source Section6 Conjecture2 states all n, but K4 is C5-free and has 4 triangles+3 four-cycles=7, while K2,2 has 1 cycle. This only exposes the missing large-n qualification suggested by the surrounding extremal-edge discussion.
329595.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Large-n problem survives; need an injection/compression comparing arbitrary C(2k+1)-free graphs to balanced bipartite graphs. Tiny n correction is ineligible.

329596.title: The delta-process tree probability conjecture
329596.literal_statement:
Let $k$ and $r$ be positive integers with $r<k$, let $\textbf{p}=(p_1,\ldots,p_k)$ be a tuple of non-negative integers, and let $\mathcal{R}_{\textbf{p},r}$ be the specified set of $r$-tuples of subsets. Suppose this set is non-empty. Choose $\textbf{S}=(S_1,\ldots,S_r)$ uniformly from $\mathcal{R}_{\textbf{p},r}$ and choose a surjection $f:[k-1]\to[r]$ uniformly and independently of $\textbf{S}$. Let $G_\delta(\textbf{S},f)$ be the random digraph defined by the delta rule, and write $P_\delta(\textbf{p},r)$ for the probability that it is a tree.

**The delta-process tree probability conjecture.** One has

$$
P_\delta(\textbf{p},r)=\frac{|\mathcal{R}_{\textbf{p},r-1}|}{|\mathcal{R}_{\textbf{p},r}|}.
$$

This is equal to the probability that $S_1=\emptyset$.

The paper states that this conjecture suggests a simple expression for the tree probability and reports that it could not be proved. It is equivalent there to an identity involving a generalized probabilistic determinant.
329596.findings: Neither delta rule nor R(p,r) is specified in the normalized statement. A ratio of cardinalities is not a definition of a random-tree event.
329596.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Recover delta-rule fibers from source and construct a measure-preserving tree-event/empty-first-set bijection; no such bijection available.

329602.title: Park–Shahabi Rubin–Stark determinant and nonvanishing conjecture
329602.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{S}^{E,p}_{\infty}$ be the cyclic $\Lambda$-module generated by the tower of Rubin–Stark elements after localization and twisting, let $\Gamma_n=\operatorname{Gal}(F_n/F)$, and let $\mathfrak{d}_{n,i}$, $\mathfrak{u}_{i,j}$, $\tau(\chi)$, $\omega_n^{\epsilon}$, and $L(E/F^+,\chi,s)$ be as defined in the paper, with $\epsilon$ the sign of $(-1)^n$. **Park–Shahabi conjecture.** (i) There exists a generator $\Xi_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\Xi_g$ of $\mathcal{S}^{E,p}_{\infty}$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$, primitive character $\chi:\operatorname{Gal}(F_n/F)\to\boldsymbol{\mu}_{p^\infty}$, and positive integer $k$, the determinant identity displayed in the source holds. (ii) For all but finitely many characters $\chi$ of $\Gamma_{\mathrm{cyc}}$, one has $L(E/F^+,\chi,1)\ne0$. This conjecture predicts an explicit regulator determinant formula for the Rubin–Stark tower together with generic nonvanishing of the twisted complex $L$-values; the source gives no resolution status.
329602.findings: Displayed determinant is omitted and Rubin–Stark elements depend on substantial unformalized arithmetic hypotheses. Generic nonvanishing alone does not settle part(i).
329602.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Recover exact determinant and hypotheses, then prove the tower generator identity and nonvanishing without assuming them.

329608.title: Concavity of coverage probability in tier association probabilities
329608.literal_statement: Let $K$) be the number of tiers, and let $A_i$ denote the tier-association probability for tier $i$, with $A_i\geq 0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{K}A_i=1$. Let $P_c^*$ be the maximum overall coverage probability obtained by optimizing over these association probabilities, where the coverage expression is the one derived in Theorem. **Coverage concavity conjecture.** The probability of coverage in a multi-tier network considering handoff derived in Theorem is concave with respect to $\{A_i\}_{i=1}^{K}$. The conjecture would make the coverage-maximization problem a concave optimization problem and therefore enable efficient solution methods; the source provides numerical evidence for concavity over a wide range of system parameters but no proof.
329608.findings: Actual Theorem4 proof Eq28 supplies a double integral. A high-displacement asymptotic makes that literal approximate formula nonconcave. But Corollary2 explicitly assumes v much smaller than connection distance; high-v use may be only an invalid-domain correction. See COVERAGE.md.
329608.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Resolve whether unrestricted formula is the intended mathematical scope; otherwise prove or refute concavity within a quantitative small-displacement regime. No exact Lean endpoint or candidate credit.
primary_bodies_read: 1501.01668 Corollary2 proof; Theorem4 Eq26–29 proof; Conjecture1

329651.title: Chihara's conjecture on the essential spectrum of Jacobi matrices
329651.literal_statement:
Let $C$ be a self-adjoint Jacobi matrix, let $b_n\to\infty$, and suppose that the smallest point $\rho$ of $\sigma_{ess}(C)$ is finite. Assume

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n^2}{b_n b_{n+1}}=\frac14.
$$

**Chihara's conjecture.** The essential spectrum satisfies

$$
\sigma_{ess}(C)=[\rho,\infty).
$$

Chihara proved under these assumptions that the zeros of the associated orthogonal polynomials are dense in $[\rho,\infty)$; the conjecture asks for the corresponding full description of the essential spectrum.
329651.findings: The normalized reference misattributes a refutation: source Section5.1 says Roehner–Valent Conjecture1 is false without extra assumptions. Actual Chihara Conjecture2 in Section5.2 is still posed, with Theorem6 sufficient conditions only. No Chihara refutation established.
329651.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Either prove quarter-class assumptions force interval essential spectrum without Theorem6 extra hypotheses, or construct a genuine spectral-gap example satisfying all quarter-class assumptions.
primary_bodies_read: 1501.03420 ConjectureA; Section5.1 refutation paragraph; Section5.2 Theorem5, Conjecture2, Theorem6

329670.title: Nonrealizability conjecture for supersolvable arrangements with a triple-point line
329670.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal A\subset\mathbb P^2$ be a full-rank supersolvable arrangement of $n$ lines with a singular modular point $P$ of maximum multiplicity $m\geq 3$. A line has only triple singularities when every singular point on it has multiplicity $3$. **Nonrealizability conjecture.** If there exists a line $\ell\in\mathcal A$ not passing through $P$ and having only triple singularities, then $\mathcal A$ is not realizable over $\mathbb C$.

This is proposed as a route toward the complex supersolvable Dirac–Motzkin conjecture: establishing the nonrealizability assertion would rule out the configurations needed for a line away from the modular point to have no simple points. The paper does not prove the assertion in general.
329670.findings: Modularity forces all intersections onto lines through P; a line with triple singularities partitions its intersections into pairs of other lines. Incidence counting alone does not imply complex nonrealizability.
329670.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Derive incompatible complex cross-ratio/product equations from the pairing arrangement. No realization obstruction proved.

329677.title: Polylogarithmic gaps conjecture for the 6-GP-free process
329677.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be the sequence generated by the $6$-GP-free process, and interpret a gap of size $O((\log x)^C)$ as the existence of a constant implicit in the big-$O$ bound, independent of $x$. **Polylogarithmic gaps conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, with nonzero probability, the sequence $T$ has gaps of size

$$
O((\log x)^C).
$$

The conjecture proposes a substantial improvement over the paper's main bound and is motivated by the expected polylogarithmic scale of the largest gaps in the prime and squarefree sequences. It would give short gaps for a GP-free sequence while avoiding the unresolved distributional difficulties associated with those classical sequences.
329677.findings: A deterministic GP-free set with polylogarithmic gaps would not show positive probability for this specific random process.
329677.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Obtain uniform lower-tail estimates and summability for empty intervals of the actual 6-GP process.

329695.title: The bounded-support-point conjecture for normalized Loewner mappings
329695.literal_statement: Let $S^0(\mathcal D_n)$ be the compact class of normalized mappings generated by Loewner chains, and call $f\in S^0(\mathcal D_n)$ a **support point** if a nonconstant real part of a continuous linear functional attains its maximum at $f$. **Bounded-support-point conjecture.** If $f\in S^0(\mathcal D_n)$ is bounded, then $f$ is not a support point of $S^0(\mathcal D_n)$. In one complex variable the analogous support points are unbounded; the assertion is presented as open in higher dimensions.
329695.findings: Compactness of S0 does not exclude bounded maximizers of arbitrary continuous linear functionals. One-variable analogy is not a proof.
329695.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Construct an admissible Loewner-chain perturbation increasing every candidate exposing functional; deformation must remain in S0.

329707.title: Conjecture on localization of self-reinforced diffusions with trigonometric interaction
329707.literal_statement:
Let $(X_t)_{t\geqslant 0}$ solve the stochastic differential equation

$$
dX_t=\sigma\,dW_t+\sum_{k=1}^{n}ka_k\int_0^t\sin(k(X_t-X_s))\,ds\,dt,\qquad X_0=x.
$$

**Self-reinforced diffusion conjecture.** If $\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^2a_k<0$, then $X_t$ converges almost surely; if $\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^2a_k>0$, then

$$
\limsup_{t\to\infty}X_t>\liminf_{t\to\infty}X_t.
$$

The sign of the derivative of the interaction drift at zero is expected to determine whether the diffusion localizes or continues to fluctuate. The preceding analysis proves almost-sure convergence for the single-frequency model, while the corresponding assertion for the general self-reinforced diffusion is posed here as an open conjecture.
329707.findings: The interaction near zero has derivative sum k^2 a_k, but controlling only this derivative does not control global trapping or the long-memory stochastic drift.
329707.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Prove a global localization criterion from the local derivative for arbitrary trigonometric mixtures, with almost-sure quantifier.

329711.title: Yang–Mills characterization conjecture for regular Markovian holonomy fields
329711.literal_statement: Let ${\sf HF}$ be a regular Markovian holonomy field, and let an admissible Lévy process determine a Yang–Mills field through the Yang–Mills-fields construction. **Yang–Mills characterization conjecture.** Every regular Markovian holonomy field is a Yang–Mills field. This would show that the two arrows between regular Markovian holonomy fields and admissible Lévy processes are inverse to each other, completing the characterization of regular Markovian holonomy fields by admissible Lévy processes. The source does not state a resolution of this conjecture.
329711.findings: Having maps in both directions between fields and Levy processes does not establish inverse equivalence.
329711.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Prove uniqueness of the field from disk holonomies under the full regularity/Markov/gluing axioms.

329765.title: Linear-density partial-sum sequencing problem
329765.literal_statement:
Let $A$ be a $k$-element subset of the nonzero elements of ${\mathbb Z}_n$, and let the partial-sum sequencing conjecture be the assertion that $A$ has an ordering with pairwise distinct partial sums. **Linear-density sequencing problem.** Find a constant $c$ such that

$$
k\leq cn
$$

implies that the partial-sum sequencing conjecture holds. This asks for a uniform positive-density range in which the main conjecture can be proved. The source presents it as a generalization of the preceding conjectures and gives no value of $c$ or resolution.
329765.findings: A density argument in cyclic groups cannot discard small subgroups; an obstruction at modulus m embeds into arbitrarily large multiples. Fixed k or prime-modulus theorems do not imply this question. In fact any positive uniform density theorem implies the full main conjecture by the same injective scaling; proof retained.
329765.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Prove sequencing uniformly for dense subsets in every cyclic group, including sets contained in proper subgroups.

329766.title: Fixed-size partial-sum sequencing problem
329766.literal_statement:
Let $k$ be fixed, and let $A$ be a $k$-element subset of the nonzero elements of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. **Fixed-size sequencing problem.** Determine whether there exists a constant $N$ such that, whenever

$$
n\geq N,
$$

the partial-sum sequencing conjecture holds for $A$. This is a fixed-$k$, large-$n$ generalization of the main conjecture. The source states the problem but supplies no proof, value of $N$, or resolution.
329766.findings: For fixed k, large-n conclusion is equivalent to the all-moduli statement by injective scaling Z_m -> Z_(tm). Retained proof in MATHEMATICAL-NOTES.md. So asymptotic rectification alone cannot bypass bounded torsion.
329766.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Settle all cyclic groups for arbitrary fixed k, not only primes with large least prime factor.

329787.title: Hopkins's equivariant presentation conjecture for the Morava $E$-theory homotopy groups
329787.literal_statement:
Let $K\subset \mathbb{S}_n$ be a finite subgroup. Let $\rho\in E_n$ be placed in degree $-2$, let $S(\rho)$ denote the graded symmetric algebra, let $N$ be a trivial representation corresponding to the multiplicative norm over the group on $\rho$, and let $I$ be an ideal in degree $0$. **Hopkins's conjecture.** There is a $K$-equivariant isomorphism

$$
(E_n)_*\simeq S_{\mathbb{W}(\mathbb{F}_{p^n})}(\rho)[N^{-1}]^\wedge_I.
$$

This conjectural presentation is intended to make the action of finite subgroups on $(E_n)_*$ easier to describe and compute, supporting calculations involving the homotopy fixed-point and Tate spectra of higher real $K$-theories. The source presents it as Hopkins's conjecture, and no resolution is given here.
329787.findings: Equivariant completed graded algebra presentation requires actual finite-subgroup action and integral deformation coordinates.
329787.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Construct equivariant coordinates and prove I-adic completion/localization matches all homotopy groups.

329805.title: Necessary conditions for divisibility of two-part-size partition counts
329805.literal_statement:
Let $\nu_2(m)$ denote the relevant counting function for partitions into two sizes of part, and let $A$ and $B$ be integers such that $An+B$ is the progression under consideration. Let $\sigma_1(m)$ be the sum-of-divisors function, let $d(m)$ be the auxiliary function used in the paper, and say that a progression contains sums of two squares if some integer in it is a sum of two squares. **Necessary-conditions conjecture.** If

$$
\nu_2(An+B)\equiv 0\pmod{4}
$$

for all $n$, then for all $n$,

$$
\sigma_1(An+B)\equiv 0\pmod{8},\qquad d(An+B)\equiv d\left(\frac{An+B}{2}\right)^2\pmod{8},
$$

and the progression $An+B$ never contains sums of two squares. These conditions are conjectured to be necessary for such a divisibility progression; the source notes that they are not known to be exhaustive and that computation had not found a counterexample.
329805.findings: Read source Conjecture1 and preceding modular-form proof. Existing sufficiency proofs for four progressions do not imply necessity for every progression. A finite list of coefficients cannot certify the premise.
329805.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Either derive each divisor/sums-of-squares condition from an identically vanishing modular progression, or prove a new progression identity violating one condition.

329822.title: Optimality of extremely branched trees for the Basic regression
329822.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{R}(n)$ be the class of trees on $n$ vertices, and let $BP^0$ denote the Basic regression with minimum value $BP^{0*}_\mathcal{R}(n)$ over $\mathcal{R}(n)$. A tree is **pendent-rooted** when its root is a pendent vertex, and an **extremely branched tree** is the tree type depicted in the paper's minimizing-tree figure. **Extremely branched tree conjecture.** If

$$
BP^0(T)=BP^{0*}_\mathcal{R}(n)
$$

for some pendent-rooted tree $T\in\mathcal{R}(n)$, then $T$ is an extremely branched tree.
The claim formalizes the paper's hypothesis that an extremely branched tree optimizes the Basic regression, although the authors explain that they cannot prove this from the available inequalities for the ad hoc index $C^0$.
329822.findings: Extremely branched is figure-defined and BP0 depends on an ad hoc regression functional; standard degree-majorization arguments do not identify its minimizer.
329822.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Recover exact functional then prove a strict tree surgery reducing it for each non-extremely-branched pendent-rooted tree.

329827.title: Effective finiteness conjecture for rational matrix families
329827.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be any finite set of square matrices with rational entries, and let $\overline\rho_k(\mathcal F)$ denote the maximum normalized spectral radius among products of length $k$. **Effective finiteness conjecture.** There exists an effectively computable natural number $t(\mathcal F)$ such that

$$
\overline\rho_{t(\mathcal F)}(\mathcal F)=\rho(\mathcal F).
$$

The source states that Blondel and Tsitsiklis proved this conjecture false, so no such effective bound exists in the asserted generality.
329827.findings: Source discusses effective finiteness and its prior disproof by Blondel–Tsitsiklis. Computability is central, so a single product example does not even match the effective assertion.
329827.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: No discovery route from a new finite-matrix computation.

329863.title: The negative Houghton-group Sigma-invariant conjecture
329863.literal_statement:
Let $(H_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be the Houghton groups. For $n\geq 2$, let $\chi_1,\dots,\chi_n$ be the characters defined by the eventual translation lengths, with $\chi_1+\cdots+\chi_n=0$. For a non-trivial character

$$
\chi=a_1\chi_1+\cdots+a_n\chi_n,
$$

where the $a_i$ are not all equal, reorder the coefficients so that $a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_n$, and let $m(\chi)$ be maximal with $1\leq m(\chi)\leq n-1$ and $a_{m(\chi)}\neq a_n$. **Negative Houghton-group Sigma-invariant conjecture.** With this setup, moreover

$$
[\chi]\notin\Sigma^{m(\chi)}(H_n).
$$

The preceding theorem proves the complementary positive result $[\chi]\in\Sigma^{m(\chi)-1}(H_n)$; the conjecture would determine the relevant boundary of the higher Bieri–Neumann–Strebel–Renz invariants. It remains open in the source.
329863.findings: Zaremsky1808.00634v2 Theorem2.3 is exactly [chi] not in Sigma^m(chi). Section4 blankets/nerve proof inspected. Same sorted-character definition; no parameter restriction saves novelty.
329863.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: No new proof requested; later primary theorem directly resolves target.

329868.title: Sharp order of growth for the minimum degree of minimal Ramsey graphs for triangles
329868.literal_statement:
Let $s_r(K_3)$ denote the minimum degree of an $r$-edge-coloured graph that is minimal Ramsey for the triangle $K_3$. **Triangle-case conjecture.**

$$
s_r(K_3)=\Theta\left(r^2\ln r\right).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the paper's lower bound for the triangle case is tight, motivated by the possibility of packing edge-disjoint triangle-free graphs with independence number $O(\sqrt{n\ln n})$. The source gives no resolution of this conjecture.
329868.findings: Need matching upper bound O(r^2 log r) for minimal Ramsey triangle degree, not merely a Ramsey graph or a packing with uncontrolled minimum degree.
329868.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Construct the required edge-disjoint triangle-free packings with uniform independence bound and bridge to minimal Ramsey graphs.

329886.title: The minimum-degree conjecture for disjoint long cycles
329886.literal_statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and $r\geq 3$ be integers. A collection of cycles is **disjoint** when its cycles have pairwise disjoint vertex sets.

**Long-cycle packing conjecture.** Every graph with minimum degree at least

$$
\tfrac{2}{3}kr
$$

and at least $kr$ vertices contains $k$ disjoint cycles, each containing at least $r$ vertices.

The conjecture would imply the paper's average-degree result and would directly generalize the cited minimum-degree theorem of Corrádi and Hajnal. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
329886.findings: Minimum degree 2kr/3 exceeds known cycle existence bounds but does not survive deleting long cycles of uncontrolled length.
329886.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Find a bounded-length cycle deletion or absorption lemma preserving the degree threshold for k-1 cycles.

329887.title: Hwang's odd-cycle packing conjecture
329887.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k\geq 2$ and odd $r\geq 3$ be integers.

**Hwang's odd-cycle packing conjecture.** If $G$ has at least $rk$ vertices and minimum degree at least

$$
\tfrac{r+1}{2}k,
$$

then $G$ contains $k$ disjoint cycles, each containing at least $r$ vertices.

The conjecture is one of two minimum-degree extensions attributed to Hwang. The supplied text presents it as open and explains that its degree threshold is forced by a split-graph construction.
329887.findings: Odd r refers to threshold parameter, not parity of the packed cycles. Testing graphs without odd cycles would be a semantic error.
329887.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Prove k vertex-disjoint cycles each of length at least r at exact minimum degree (r+1)k/2.

329888.title: Hwang's even-cycle packing conjecture
329888.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k\geq 3$ and even $r\geq 6$ be integers.

**Hwang's even-cycle packing conjecture.** If $G$ has at least $rk$ vertices and minimum degree at least

$$
\tfrac{r}{2}k,
$$

then $G$ contains $k$ disjoint cycles, each containing at least $r$ vertices, unless $k$ is odd and

$$
rk+1\leq |V(G)|\leq rk+r-2.
$$

The exceptional range is explained in the source by disjoint unions of two cliques, which can meet the degree requirement without containing the required cycle packing. The conjecture is presented as open.
329888.findings: The stated exceptional interval already removes the two-clique obstruction. Reusing that obstruction inside the interval does not refute the implication.
329888.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Find a packing obstruction outside the exceptional order interval or prove a degree-partition theorem at rk/2.

329889.title: The average-degree conjecture for even long-cycle packings
329889.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k\geq 3$ and even $r\geq 6$ be integers.

**Even average-degree cycle-packing conjecture.** If $G$ has average degree at least

$$
rk-2
$$

and at least $rk$ vertices, then $G$ contains $k$ disjoint cycles, each containing at least $r$ vertices.

This is proposed as an average-degree weakening of Hwang's even-cycle packing conjecture. The source explains that the average-degree formulation avoids the disjoint-union obstruction relevant to the minimum-degree version and presents the conjecture as open.
329889.findings: Average degree rk-2 is much stronger than min-degree hypothesis in the companion conjecture. Disjoint undersized cliques do not meet this average-degree requirement.
329889.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Obtain a cycle-packing-preserving dense core, or a sharp extremal edge bound for graphs with packing number <k.

329898.title: Optimality conjecture for trivariate Lissajous curve frequency triples
329898.literal_statement:
Let $(a,b,c)$ be a triple of strictly positive integers, and let $c_n$ be the largest entry of the frequency triple specified by the paper's equation. Assume

$$
\max\{a,b,c\}<c_n.
$$

**Optimality conjecture.** There exists an integer triple $(i,j,k)$, not all zero, with $i+j+k\leq 2n$, such that at least one of

$$
ia=jb+kc,\qquad jb=ia+kc,\qquad kc=ia+jb
$$

holds. Equivalently, the triples specified by are precisely those satisfying the conclusion of Theorem 1 with the minimum possible maximum frequency.

The conjecture asserts that the frequency triples in give optimal rank-1 Chebyshev lattices for the stated cubature degree. The supplied text does not indicate whether this optimality claim has been proved or disproved.
329898.findings: Read Theorem1, its constructive proof, Conjecture1, lattice-kernel Lemma1 and Siegel Lemma2; Bos2017 recipe/proof context is not an optimality theorem. Exact integer search n1..8 found no shorter-max-frequency witness; diagnostic only.
329898.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Prove every positive triple with max<c_n has a nonzero integer kernel vector of l1 norm <=2n. Source Siegel bound has insufficient sharp constant. Need sharp two-dimensional lattice geometry or a larger exact counterexample.
primary_bodies_read: 1502.04114 Theorem1 appendix constructive proof, Lemmas1–2 and Conjecture1; Bos2017 Proposition0.1 and recipe

329918.title: The alternative conjecture on the spectral norm of Gaussian random matrices
329918.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be the $d\times d$ symmetric random matrix with entries $X_{ij}=b_{ij}g_{ij}$, where $\{g_{ij}:i\ge j\}$ are independent standard Gaussian random variables and $\{b_{ij}:i\ge j\}$ are given nonnegative scalars. For a symmetric matrix, $X^2$ denotes its square, and $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the operator norm. **Alternative spectral-norm conjecture.** The expected spectral norm satisfies

$$
\mathbf{E}\|X\|\asymp\|\mathbf{E}X^2\|^{1/2}+\mathbf{E}\max_{ij}|X_{ij}|.
$$

This formulation is motivated by a dimension-dependent upper bound whose first term equals $\|\mathbf{E}X^2\|^{1/2}$ and whose second term controls the expected largest entry. The source presents it as an alternative to Latała's conjecture and does not provide a resolution.
329918.findings: Latała-type norm comparison quantifies dimension-free constants over all variance profiles. Single diagonal/block examples are consistent and cannot prove or disprove comparability.
329918.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Produce an unbounded-ratio family or prove a universal upper estimate from row variance and expected maximum entry.

329938.title: The eventual quasi-polynomial conjecture for the parametric Frobenius problem
329938.literal_statement:
Let $a_i:bbZ_+crightarrowbbZ_+$, $1cle icle n$, be eventually positive functions in $cmathrm{EQP}$, where $F(a_1,cdots,a_n)$ denotes the largest element of the group $cmathbb{Z}a_1+cdots+cmathbb{Z}a_n$ not in the semigroup generated by $a_1,cdots,a_n$. A function is in $cmathrm{EQP}$ if it eventually agrees with a quasi-polynomial. **The parametric Frobenius conjecture.** Then

$$
Fcbig(a_1(t),cdots,a_n(t)cbig)cincmathrm{EQP}.
$$

The conjecture predicts eventual quasi-polynomial behavior for Frobenius numbers whose generators vary as eventual quasi-polynomial functions. The paper proves this in the special cases where the generators are linear functions or where $ncle 3$, while the general case remains open.
329938.findings: Shen1510.01349 Theorem1.5 with m=l=1 gives the generalized Frobenius EQP conclusion; source explicitly notes residue-class reduction for EQP generators. Proof reduction not read in full; theorem-level subsumption already disqualifies novelty.
329938.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: No discovery route; residue-class substitution and finite common period are routine.
primary_bodies_read: 1502.06009 conjecture; 1510.01349 Theorem1.5 and EQP reduction paragraph

329950.title: Teschner's conjecture on the upper bondage number of critical graphs
329950.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{P} \subseteq \mathcal{G}$ be additive and hereditary. A graph $G$ is **vertex-$\gamma_{\mathcal{P}}$-critical** if its vertex domination number with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ has the criticality property used in the paper, and let $b_{\mathcal{P}}^+(G)$ denote its upper bondage number and $\Delta(G)$ its maximum degree. **Teschner's conjecture.** For any vertex-$\gamma_{\mathcal{P}}$-critical graph $G$, 

$$
b_{\mathcal{P}}^+(G) \leq 1.5\Delta(G).
$$

The conjecture is presented as the main outstanding conjecture on the ordinary bondage number when $\mathcal{P}=\mathcal{G}$; its general status is not resolved in the supplied source.
329950.findings: General additive hereditary domination property P is part of the endpoint. Ordinary domination bounds do not automatically transport to arbitrary P.
329950.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Recover vertex criticality and upper-bondage definitions; prove an edge-deletion witness bounded by 3 Delta/2 preserving property-sensitive domination.

329980.title: The Pressing Game Conjecture on successful pressing sequences
329980.literal_statement:
Let $(G,c)$ be a bicolored graph, where a press may be performed only at a black vertex, and call a sequence of presses **successful** if it transforms $(G,c)$ into an all-white, empty graph. **Pressing Game Conjecture.** Every successful pressing sequence can be reached from every other one by a sequence of edits involving at most four deletions or insertions.

This conjecture concerns the connectivity of the space of successful pressing sequences under local edits, and is motivated by the correspondence between successful pressing sequences in breakpoint graphs and minimum-length reversal-sorting sequences for signed permutations. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
329980.findings: Source binary matrix factorization criteria help recognize successful sequences but do not prove connectivity under four edits. Linear-graph companion covers only a restricted graph family.
329980.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Prove bounded-size exchange connecting any two symmetric Gaussian-elimination orders, including singular matrices; no exchange lemma established.

330013.title: Transfer-operator eigenfunctions determining resonance residues
330013.literal_statement: Let $\Gamma_\lambda$ be the Hecke triangle group, let $\chi$ be a unitary finite-dimensional representation, and let $\mathcal L_{s,\chi}$ be the associated transfer operator. At a resonance $s$, consider the sufficiently regular vectors in the $1$-eigenspace of $\mathcal L_{s,\chi}$. **Residue-determination conjecture.** These sufficiently regular $1$-eigenfunction vectors determine the residues at the resonance $s$. This expectation is motivated by the preceding theorems and is supported in the source by a later theorem; the supplied material does not establish that the conjecture itself is fully resolved.
330013.findings: Sufficiently regular is unspecified here, and residue vectors are not determined solely by equality of resonance and transfer spectra.
330013.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Recover regularity class and construct an inverse intertwiner carrying transfer 1-eigenspace data to resolvent Laurent residues.

330028.title: The pre-building Finsler isometric-embedding conjecture
330028.literal_statement:
Assume the hypotheses of the paper's pre-building construction: there are no BPS states, $B^{\rm pre}_{\phi}$ is the resulting pre-building, and $h:X\rightarrow B$ is a $\phi$-harmonic map to a building. Let $f:B^{\rm pre}_{\phi}\rightarrow B$ be the factorization of $h$ through the pre-building. The **Finsler distance** on an apartment is the distance used in the paper's $SL_3$ model.

**Pre-building Finsler isometric-embedding conjecture.** The factorization $f:B^{\rm pre}_{\phi}\rightarrow B$ is an isometric embedding for the Finsler distance.

This would establish the claimed universal geometric property of the pre-building and determine the metric data seen by harmonic maps. The source gives no resolution of the claim.
330028.findings: Factorization/universality as maps does not imply preservation of Finsler distance; folding may shorten paths.
330028.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Show no permitted apartment folding shortens any Finsler geodesic under no-BPS hypothesis.

330073.title: The Morse-Smale broken-trajectory lower-bound conjecture
330073.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a closed, oriented hyperbolic manifold of dimension $n+1\geq 2$, and let $f:M\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a Morse-Smale function.

**Broken-trajectory lower-bound conjecture.** We have

$$
\#(n\text{-times-broken trajectories of }-\nabla f)\geq \operatorname{const}(n)\cdot\operatorname{Vol} M.
$$

This conjecture is suggested by the relationship between maximum-multiplicity trajectories of a traversally generic negative gradient field and broken trajectories satisfying Morse-Smale transversality. It predicts a lower bound proportional to the hyperbolic volume, with a positive constant depending only on $n$; whether such a bound holds remains open.
330073.findings: Morse inequalities count critical points, not fully broken trajectories with dimension-controlled volume constant.
330073.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Construct a fundamental chain from compactified unstable manifolds with l1 norm bounded by a constant times the trajectory count.

330075.title: The locating-number conjecture for twin-free graphs
330075.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a twin-free graph of order $n$ with no isolated vertices. A **locating set** is a set $S$ such that every two distinct vertices outside $S$ have distinct neighborhoods in $S$; let $\gamma_L(G)$ denote the minimum cardinality of a locating set.

**Locating-number conjecture.** Every twin-free graph $G$ of order $n$ with no isolated vertices satisfies

$$
\gamma_L(G) \leq \frac{n}{2}.
$$

This is a strengthening of the corresponding locating-domination bound because a locating set need not dominate every vertex. The supplied text does not provide a resolution status for this claim, so it is recorded as open.
330075.findings: Locating sets distinguish only outside vertices and need not dominate. Normalized prose calls this a strengthening although removing domination weakens the requirement. That wording does not resolve the bound.
330075.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Construct a locating set of size floor(n/2) from twin-freeness, or give an exact twin-free counterexample; no full-scope route proved.

330079.title: Gould, Horn and Magnant's chorded-cycle packing conjecture
330079.literal_statement:
Let $c,k$ be integers with $c\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$. For an integer $r\geq 0$, an **$r$-chorded cycle** is a cycle with $r$ chords. **Gould, Horn and Magnant's conjecture.** Every graph $G$ of order at least $(c+1)k$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\geq ck$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint $\frac{(c+1)(c-2)}{2}$-chorded cycles.

This conjecture is presented as a common generalization of Corrádi–Hajnal's theorem on disjoint cycles and Hajnal–Szemerédi's theorem on disjoint complete graphs. Its resolution is not specified in the source.
330079.findings: Cycle with r chords convention must be at-least r, not induced exactly-r. Complete graph substructures are not counterexamples by having extra chords.
330079.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Find an equitable degree partition preserving enough edges to create the target chord count in each part.

330096.title: The secure domination conjecture for digraphs with minimum semidegree at least one
330096.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph of order $n$. Write $\delta^{0}$ for its minimum semidegree, and let $\gamma_{oso}(D)$ and $\gamma_{iso}(D)$ denote its open secure out-domination and secure in-domination numbers, respectively. **Secure domination conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^{0}\geq 1,
$$

then

$$
\gamma_{oso}(D)\leq \left\lceil\frac{2n}{3}\right\rceil\qquad\text{and}\qquad\gamma_{iso}(D)\leq \left\lceil\frac{2n}{3}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture proposes sharp upper bounds for two secure domination parameters in digraphs with minimum semidegree at least one; the source presents it as an open conjecture.
330096.findings: Source Propositions2.9 and5.9 prove gamma_oso(C4)=gamma_iso(C4)=3. Three disjoint C4 have order12, semidegree1, both numbers9>ceil(24/3)=8. Additivity proof retained. Immediate same-source disjoint-union corollary; no Lean investment.
330096.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Only reconsider if a separate connected/strongly-connected target is actually authorized; no such target replaces this literal record.
primary_bodies_read: 1503.04048 definitions1.3–1.4, Proposition2.9 proof, Theorem5.3 proof, Proposition5.9 proof, Conjecture6.4

330103.title: The SLP conjecture for nonequipointed linear spaces
330103.findings: Source Theorem4.10 proof gives degree>=2 block matrices, but this only proves WLP. Conjecture4.11 persists in October2015 author manuscript. SLP needs all powers, especially source degree1 incidence maps; arbitrary-field ranks cannot be inferred from positive real Gram matrices.
330103.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Determine exact ranks of point-versus-collinear-j-subset incidence matrices over every allowed characteristic; combine with rectangular Boolean-block maps. No full endpoint.
primary_bodies_read: 1503.04335 Theorem4.10 proof and Conjecture4.11; projPlanes151015 same passages

330115.title: Circuit Hirsch conjecture
330115.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional polyhedron with $f$ facets. Its **circuit diameter** is the largest circuit distance between any two vertices, where circuit walks generalize edge walks by allowing circuit directions instead of only directions corresponding to incident edges. **Circuit Hirsch conjecture.** The circuit diameter of $P$ is bounded above by

$$
f-d.
$$

Unlike the graph-diameter version of the Hirsch conjecture, which has counterexamples, the circuit-diameter bound remains unresolved in general. The cited work establishes it in a setting where Hirsch's bound fails for graph diameter, providing evidence for the conjecture.
330115.findings: Record references call graph Hirsch refutation a circuit refutation, but actual statement distinguishes them. Graph-distance counterexamples do not lower-bound circuit distance.
330115.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Compute all feasible maximal circuit steps for a candidate polyhedron and certify circuit distance >f-d.

330142.title: Gog–Magog trapezoid conjecture
330142.literal_statement: An $(m,n,k)$-Gog trapezoid is the array defined by the row, column, diagonal, and rightmost-column-bound conditions in the source; an $(m,n,k)$-Magog trapezoid is the corresponding Magog trapezoid. An entry is a **Maximum** if it equals its upper bound and a **Minimum** if it equals $1$. **Gog–Magog trapezoid conjecture.** The number of $(m,n,k)$-Magog trapezoids with $s$ Maxima in the first row and $t$ Minima in the last row equals the number of $(m,n,k)$-Gog trapezoids with $t$ Maxima in the rightmost column and $s$ Minima in the leftmost column. The conjecture proposes an equality between refined enumerations of two classes of trapezoidal arrays related to alternating sign matrices. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
330142.findings: Reference to MacMahon conjecture is unrelated to the refined Gog–Magog endpoint. Unrefined counting is insufficient.
330142.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Construct a refinement-preserving bijection or prove bivariate generating-function equality for arbitrary m,n,k.

330171.title: The largest-Laplacian-eigenvalue conjecture for Hamming graphs
330171.literal_statement:
Let $H(d,q,j)$ be the Hamming graph on $q^d$ vertices, with two vertices adjacent when their Hamming distance is $j$. Write

$$
\lambda=q(q-1)^{j-1}{d-1 \choose j-1}.
$$

**Largest-Laplacian-eigenvalue conjecture.** If $q\geq 2$ and $j\geq d-\frac{d-1}{q}$, with $j$ even if $q=2$, then $\lambda$ is the largest Laplacian eigenvalue of $H(d,q,j)$.
This conjecture identifies the Laplacian eigenvalue arising from the common Hamming-scheme idempotent as the extremal one in the stated parameter range, extending the known max-cut result for the relevant binary Hamming graphs. Its general status is not established in the supplied source.
330171.findings: Brouwer–Cioaba–Ihringer–McGinnis1709.09011 Theorem1.4 plus binary Corollary1.3 settle smallest adjacency eigenvalue; subtract from regular degree to obtain literal Laplacian maximum. Recurrence proof in Section2.2 inspected.
330171.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: No novelty route: degree-K_j(1)=q(q-1)^(j-1) choose(d-1,j-1), matching target.
primary_bodies_read: 1709.09011 Conjecture1.1, Theorems1.2/1.4, Corollary1.3, Section2.2 recurrence proof

330180.title: Eigenstate thermalisation hypothesis
330180.literal_statement:
Let $A$ be a few-body observable, and let $|E_k\rangle$ be an eigenvector of the Hamiltonian of a large interacting many-body system with energy $E_k$. **Eigenstate thermalisation hypothesis.** The expectation value of $A$ in this eigenvector equals the thermal average of $A$ at the mean energy $E_k$:

$$
\langle E_k|A|E_k\rangle = \langle A\rangle_{\mathrm{thermal},E_k}.
$$

The ETH is a central proposed explanation for why closed interacting quantum systems can exhibit thermal behaviour, asserting that individual energy eigenstates reproduce thermal expectation values for few-body observables. The source states the hypothesis but gives no resolution status.
330180.findings: Universal exact ETH fails for familiar conserved/integrable systems and for finite-size exact equality. Generic thermodynamic ETH is not a theorem with the literal finite quantifiers. Such examples would be known-phenomenon/domain corrections.
330180.decisive_next_lemma_or_action: Require a precise genuinely new Hamiltonian class and limit statement before formalization; do not count a diagonal-matrix example.
